about: The `report_anomalies` table, published whole. See /api/schema for its grain. This file is fy 2015 only.

rows.detail: The Salary Schedule for FY2016 is announced by heading on p198 and then simply not printed -- the grade/step dollar grid is missing from the document, while the classification list that references it is complete.
Selectmen appear at $100.00 each; the Superintendent at $136,578.97; the Town Manager appears twice under different names (LAFLEUR is absent, SPEIDEL KERRY TOWN MANAGER 130,102.20).
A record of which boards were active in 2015 -- the Building Reuse Committee and School Building Committee, both active per pp11 and 15, are absent from this schedule.

rows.table: Fire department call volume by type
rows.detail: These sum to 1,980, not the 1,985 stated -- the breakdown does not tie to its own printed total.

Roughly ten pages of the town meeting section (pp144-153, and again pp154-166) reprint the same Architectural Preservation District bylaw and Village Center District zoning bylaw twice over -- the as-submitted and as-amended texts both in full, without either being labelled as a duplicate.

rows.table: Annual town meeting article votes, May 2, 2015
rows.detail: NOTE: the APD bylaw text appears TWICE (pp144-148 as Article 26's motion and pp149-153 as the amended version), and the Village Center parking and dimensional tables appear twice as well (p157 and p163) -- roughly ten pages of this section are a near-duplicate of another ten.

Two of the biggest tables carry their page title at the BOTTOM of the page rather than the top: the FY2015 receipts table (p22) and the Treasurer's cash statement (p37, whose total line dates itself 6/30/14 while the heading says 6/30/2015). The employee compensation table (pp206-211) has no heading at all.
The heading 'FY 2016 Omnibus Budget' prints only once, at the top left of p140; p141 carries no heading at all.
THIS TABLE HAS NO HEADING AND NO PRINTED TOTAL -- a heading-driven search will not find it at all.

Page 87 carries a benchmarking chart comparing Lunenburg's police arrests, incidents and officer counts against twelve named Massachusetts towns with their populations -- a peer-comparison dataset in a town report, and one whose numbers cannot be reattached to their towns from the text layer.

The election results on pp201-202 do not internally reconcile: the School Committee contest prints a TOTAL row of 4,034 votes while its own candidate rows sum to 247, and the Cemetery Commissioner's winning candidate is credited with 1,478 votes in a contest whose TOTAL row says 247.

The special education report on p103 publishes exactly the out-of-district placement COUNT that dollar-based analysis cannot recover -- thirty students as of 1 March 2015, split nine collaborative, fifteen day, six residential.
The fire department's own call breakdown does not sum to its own stated total: 483 + 967 + 493 + 37 = 1,980 against a stated 1,985 calls.
The DPW report states the town has 86 miles of paved streets while the town profile on p6 says 'ROAD MILES- ABOUT 100'.

rows.table: Assessor's overlay, exemptions and abatements, five years
rows.detail: One row label is stale: 'Charges to 6/30/2010' heads a column series running through FY2015 -- the label was not updated when the table was rolled forward.

The report contains three different district enrollment totals on three consecutive pages (1,595 as of 19 Feb 2016 on p101; 1,567 on p103; 503 for the Primary School as of 1 Oct 2015 on p105 against 516 in the p101 table), each measured on a different date and none of them flagged as different.

rows.table: District enrollment by grade and residency
rows.detail: Three different enrollment totals in three adjacent pages, each measured on a different date.
THREE separate rosters under three different headings, spanning six pages -- a heading search for one form of the phrase will find some and miss others.

rows.table: Lunenburg High School MCAS results, grades 8 and 10
rows.detail: Grade 8 is tested at the HIGH SCHOOL here (grade 8 was housed at LHS in this configuration) while grades 4-7 were at the middle school -- so the district's MCAS results are split across three separate tables on three pages under three different headings, with different column names each time.

rows.table: Annual town election results by precinct
rows.detail: The data is internally inconsistent and should be treated with care: SCHOOL COMMITTEE prints 'TOTAL 1128 872 964 1070 4034' while its candidate, all-others and blanks rows sum to 247;

rows.table: FY2016 elected officials by term expiry
rows.detail: This list differs from the p9-10 elected officials list, which is the pre-election slate -- the report carries both.

Department codes are free text and inconsistent: SCHOOL, POLICE, FIRE, DPW, COA, LIBRARY, ACCT, IT, PARK, CEMETERY, BUILDING, HEALTH, WIRING, PLUMB/GAS, LAND USE, PLANNING, SELECTMEN, REGISTRATIONS, TOWN MANAGER, VETERAN SERV, TAX WORKOFF.
The DPW report on p56 separately says '86 miles of paved streets' -- two different road-mile figures in one document.

rows.table: Salary schedule for fiscal year 2016 -- HEADING ONLY, TABLE ABSENT
rows.detail: This is a genuine omission, not an OCR failure -- p198 is 'plain' mode with 16 recovered lines and the next page (199) starts the next town meeting article.
Reading order interleaves the three columns, so a naive line parse mixes unrelated sources.

rows.table: Assessments and revenues by major property class
rows.detail: The Industrial valuation prints as '20,155.100' with a decimal point where a comma belongs (an OCR or typesetting error); the value should read 20,155,100 for the column to sum to the printed total.
